name: FilmCraft
description: Headless video editor (FilmCraft from ArtCraft, open source, written in Rust). Imports MP4, MOV, WebM and MKV video, WAV/MP3 audio and still images, builds sequences on a multi-track timeline, cuts, trims and places clips, adds titles and shapes, transitions, effects, color grading (Lumetri), audio mixing and captions, runs any of its 700+ editor commands, renders PNG frames and exports H.264 MP4, ProRes/DNxHR MOV, GIF, WAV and MP3.
instructions:
FilmCraft runs headless in your own container; every file lives in /work.

1. Upload the clips, audio and stills to /work and import them: media_import {"paths":["/work/a.mp4","/work/b.mp4"]} returns their item ids (e.g. [1,2]).
2. Create a sequence from the first clip, so its size and frame rate are taken over: command_run {"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"cut","fromItem":1}}.
3. Put the clips on the timeline one after another: command_run {"id":"timeline.place","params":{"items":[1,2],"track":"V1","seconds":0,"insert":false}}.
4. Edit. A title for 3 s: command_run {"id":"graphics.newText","params":{"text":"Hello","seconds":3,"time":0,"track":"new","size":72}}. Everything else is an engine command: command_list {"filter":"razor"} (also "transition", "effects", "graphics", "audio", "lumetri", "captions"…) — always pass a filter, the registry has 700+ commands — then command_run {"id":...,"params":{...}}, or command_batch {"steps":[...]} for several. Times are in seconds ("seconds") or ticks (254016000000 per second).
5. Check the result: sequence_inspect shows tracks, clips and their ids; render_preview {"seconds":1} saves a PNG of that frame into /work and returns its path (no inline image) — download it to look at it or to show it.
6. Export: command_run {"id":"file.exportMedia","params":{"path":"/work/out.mp4","wait":true}} renders H.264/AAC MP4 and returns when the file is written (without "wait":true it returns at once; poll command_run {"id":"jobs.list"} then). Other formats with "format": "prores" or "dnxhr" (.mov), "gif", "wav", "mp3". WebM export is not available. Use a new file name for every export. To continue editing later: command_run {"id":"file.saveAs","params":{"path":"/work/<name>.fcproj"}} and file.open it in a later session.
7. Hand the result over: download it from /work with plugin_download_file.

All paths must be inside /work; relative paths resolve against /work. A new MCP session (e.g. after a reconnect) starts with an empty project, so save .fcproj files after each stage and reopen them then. The container and /work are deleted after the conversation is idle, so always download the results.
